addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

{"body":"Closes #492.

Adds a first-class **`write_mode: overwrite`** (full-refresh / truncate-load): each run atomically **replaces the entire destination** with its records. Writes are staged and swapped into place **only after a fully successful, uncancelled run**, so a mid-run failure or cancel leaves the previous destination completely intact.

### Not a major version bump
`WriteMode` is now `#[non_exhaustive]` (joining the transform-config extension-point enums), so adding `Overwrite` — and any future mode — is an **additive/minor** change. `cargo-semver-checks` reports *"no semver update required."*

### Core
`WriteMode::Overwrite` + four defaulted `Sink` lifecycle methods (`is_overwrite` / `begin_overwrite` / `commit_overwrite` / `abort_overwrite`) driven by `Pipeline::run` (begin before first write → commit on success → abort on failure/cancel). Forwarded through every sink decorator.

### Sinks (6 of the upsert-capable set)
| Sink | Atomic swap |
|---|---|
| postgres | transactional `TRUNCATE`+`INSERT…SELECT`+`DROP` of a `LIKE` staging clone |
| sqlite | transactional `DELETE`+`INSERT…SELECT`+`DROP` of a `SELECT…WHERE 0` clone |
| mysql | `CREATE TABLE … LIKE` + atomic `RENAME TABLE` (MySQL auto-commits DDL) |
| mssql | transactional `DELETE`+`INSERT` (explicit non-IDENTITY columns) |
| mongodb | staging collection + atomic `renameCollection(dropTarget:true)` |
| **bigquery** | **bucket-free**: query-API temp-table load + `BEGIN TRANSACTION; TRUNCATE; INSERT…SELECT; COMMIT` (preserves partitioning/clustering) |

The target must already exist (overwrite replaces rows, not schema). **Elasticsearch is intentionally excluded** — no atomic concrete-index replace exists; safe overwrite needs an alias-based redesign (follow-up).

### CLI
`write_mode: overwrite` parses; rejected at `faucet validate` on unsupported sinks and when combined with `exactly_once`, `schema.on_drift: evolve`, or scoped cleanup. Registry `OVERWRITE_SINK_KINDS` allowlist + capability-parity assertions.

### Tests
Core lifecycle (commit-on-success / abort-on-failure / abort-on-cancel / non-overwrite skip); sqlite offline; **postgres/mysql/mongodb container tests passing against real DBs** (swap + abort-safety); mssql container tests; bigquery swap-SQL builder. CLI gate + registry-parity tests. Docs, capability matrix, cookbook, 6 sink READMEs, committed JSON schema, and a runnable example all updated.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Compute patch (changed-line) coverage from an lcov report + a git diff.
3	
4	Why this exists: `codecov/patch` reports the same number, but it posts
5	unreliably — of the eight PRs merged before this script landed, only one carried
6	a `codecov/patch` status on its head commit, including a large code PR that
7	carried none. A required check that frequently never posts blocks every PR on
8	"Expected — waiting for status", so codecov cannot be the gate. This runs inside
9	the already-required `Coverage` job instead, where the result is deterministic
10	and ours.
11	
12	Usage:
13	    patch-coverage.py --lcov lcov.info --base origin/main [--min 90.0]
14	
15	Exits non-zero when coverage of added/modified lines is below `--min`, printing
16	the uncovered lines so the failure is actionable rather than just a number.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import argparse
22	import re
23	import subprocess
24	import sys
25	from collections import defaultdict
26	
27	# Kept in sync with the `--ignore-filename-regex` in the Coverage job and with
28	# codecov.yml. Paths matching these are excluded from the denominator.
29	IGNORE = re.compile(
30	    r"(/tests?/|/examples?/|/benches?/|build\.rs$"
31	    r"|crates/source/gcs/src/stream\.rs$|crates/sink/gcs/src/sink\.rs$)"
32	)
33	
34	
35	def parse_lcov(path: str) -> dict[str, dict[int, int]]:
36	    """file -> {line: hit_count} for every instrumented line."""
37	    files: dict[str, dict[int, int]] = defaultdict(dict)
38	    current: str | None = None
39	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
40	        for raw in fh:
41	            line = raw.strip()
42	            if line.startswith("SF:"):
43	                current = line[3:]
44	            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current:
45	                num, _, count = line[3:].partition(",")
46	                try:
47	                    files[current][int(num)] = int(count.split(",")[0])
48	                except ValueError:
49	                    continue
50	            elif line == "end_of_record":
51	                current = None
52	    return files
53	
54	
55	def changed_lines(base: str) -> dict[str, set[int]]:
56	    """file -> {line numbers added or modified relative to `base`}."""
57	    try:
58	        diff = subprocess.run(
59	            ["git", "diff", "--unified=0", f"{base}...HEAD", "--", "*.rs"],
60	            capture_output=True,
61	            text=True,
62	            check=True,
63	        ).stdout
64	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
65	        print(f"patch-coverage: git diff failed: {e.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
66	        sys.exit(2)
67	
68	    out: dict[str, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
69	    path: str | None = None
70	    hunk = re.compile(r"^@@ -\S+ \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@")
71	    for line in diff.splitlines():
72	        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
73	            path = line[6:]
74	        elif line.startswith("@@") and path:
75	            m = hunk.match(line)
76	            if m:
77	                start = int(m.group(1))
78	                count = int(m.group(2) or 1)
79	                out[path].update(range(start, start + count))
80	    return out
81	
82	
83	def main() -> int:
84	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
85	    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="lcov.info")
86	    ap.add_argument("--base", default="origin/main")
87	    ap.add_argument("--min", type=float, default=90.0)
88	    ap.add_argument(
89	        "--report-only",
90	        action="store_true",
91	        help="print the number but always exit 0",
92	    )
93	    args = ap.parse_args()
94	
95	    cov = parse_lcov(args.lcov)
96	    # lcov paths may be absolute; index by suffix so a repo-relative diff path
97	    # matches regardless of the workspace root.
98	    by_suffix = {p: lines for p, lines in cov.items()}
99	
100	    def lookup(rel: str) -> dict[int, int] | None:
101	        if rel in by_suffix:
102	            return by_suffix[rel]
103	        for p, lines in by_suffix.items():
104	            if p.endswith("/" + rel) or p.endswith(rel):
105	                return lines
106	        return None
107	
108	    total = 0
109	    hit = 0
110	    misses: list[str] = []
111	    for rel, lines in sorted(changed_lines(args.base).items()):
112	        if IGNORE.search(rel):
113	            continue
114	        table = lookup(rel)
115	        if table is None:
116	            # Not instrumented at all (e.g. a file excluded from the build).
117	            continue
118	        for ln in sorted(lines):
119	            if ln not in table:
120	                continue  # not an executable line (comment, brace, decl)
121	            total += 1
122	            if table[ln] > 0:
123	                hit += 1
124	            elif len(misses) < 40:
125	                misses.append(f"{rel}:{ln}")
126	
127	    if total == 0:
128	        print("patch-coverage: no instrumented changed lines; nothing to check")
129	        return 0
130	
131	    pct = 100.0 * hit / total
132	    print(f"patch-coverage: {hit}/{total} changed lines covered = {pct:.2f}%")
133

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compute patch (changed-line) coverage from an lcov report + a git diff.

Why this exists: `codecov/patch` reports the same number, but it posts
unreliably — of the eight PRs merged before this script landed, only one carried
a `codecov/patch` status on its head commit, including a large code PR that
carried none. A required check that frequently never posts blocks every PR on
"Expected — waiting for status", so codecov cannot be the gate. This runs inside
the already-required `Coverage` job instead, where the result is deterministic
and ours.

Usage:
    patch-coverage.py --lcov lcov.info --base origin/main [--min 90.0]

Exits non-zero when coverage of added/modified lines is below `--min`, printing
the uncovered lines so the failure is actionable rather than just a number.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

# Kept in sync with the `--ignore-filename-regex` in the Coverage job and with
# codecov.yml. Paths matching these are excluded from the denominator.
IGNORE = re.compile(
    r"(/tests?/|/examples?/|/benches?/|build\.rs$"
    r"|crates/source/gcs/src/stream\.rs$|crates/sink/gcs/src/sink\.rs$)"
)


def parse_lcov(path: str) -> dict[str, dict[int, int]]:
    """file -> {line: hit_count} for every instrumented line."""
    files: dict[str, dict[int, int]] = defaultdict(dict)
    current: str | None = None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
        for raw in fh:
            line = raw.strip()
            if line.startswith("SF:"):
                current = line[3:]
            elif line.startswith("DA:") and current:
                num, _, count = line[3:].partition(",")
                try:
                    files[current][int(num)] = int(count.split(",")[0])
                except ValueError:
                    continue
            elif line == "end_of_record":
                current = None
    return files


def changed_lines(base: str) -> dict[str, set[int]]:
    """file -> {line numbers added or modified relative to `base`}."""
    try:
        diff = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "diff", "--unified=0", f"{base}...HEAD", "--", "*.rs"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        ).stdout
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"patch-coverage: git diff failed: {e.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)

    out: dict[str, set[int]] = defaultdict(set)
    path: str | None = None
    hunk = re.compile(r"^@@ -\S+ \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@")
    for line in diff.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            path = line[6:]
        elif line.startswith("@@") and path:
            m = hunk.match(line)
            if m:
                start = int(m.group(1))
                count = int(m.group(2) or 1)
                out[path].update(range(start, start + count))
    return out


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--lcov", default="lcov.info")
    ap.add_argument("--base", default="origin/main")
    ap.add_argument("--min", type=float, default=90.0)
    ap.add_argument(
        "--report-only",
        action="store_true",
        help="print the number but always exit 0",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cov = parse_lcov(args.lcov)
    # lcov paths may be absolute; index by suffix so a repo-relative diff path
    # matches regardless of the workspace root.
    by_suffix = {p: lines for p, lines in cov.items()}

    def lookup(rel: str) -> dict[int, int] | None:
        if rel in by_suffix:
            return by_suffix[rel]
        for p, lines in by_suffix.items():
            if p.endswith("/" + rel) or p.endswith(rel):
                return lines
        return None

    total = 0
    hit = 0
    misses: list[str] = []
    for rel, lines in sorted(changed_lines(args.base).items()):
        if IGNORE.search(rel):
            continue
        table = lookup(rel)
        if table is None:
            # Not instrumented at all (e.g. a file excluded from the build).
            continue
        for ln in sorted(lines):
            if ln not in table:
                continue  # not an executable line (comment, brace, decl)
            total += 1
            if table[ln] > 0:
                hit += 1
            elif len(misses) < 40:
                misses.append(f"{rel}:{ln}")

    if total == 0:
        print("patch-coverage: no instrumented changed lines; nothing to check")
        return 0

    pct = 100.0 * hit / total
    print(f"patch-coverage: {hit}/{total} changed lines covered = {pct:.2f}%")

    if pct + 1e-9 < args.min and not args.report_only:
        print(f"\npatch-coverage: FAILED — below the {args.min:.2f}% floor.")
        print("Uncovered changed lines (first 40):")
        for m in misses:
            print(f"  {m}")
        print(
            "\nThe project standard is >=90% patch coverage. If a line is genuinely "
            "untestable (a signal handler, a main() dispatch arm, an infinite "
            "supervisory loop), say so explicitly in the PR rather than lowering "
            "this floor."
        )
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

aiTitle: Fix CI test coverage and improve failure reporting

content.text:
CI is running on the new commit `14d2873c`. Here's where things stand.

## What was wrong

Only the **Coverage** check was failing — everything else (including `Test`) was green. The Coverage job's custom gate reported:

```
patch-coverage: 403/517 changed lines covered = 77.95%   (floor is 90%)
```

The new `write_mode: overwrite` code was under-tested: the pipeline overwrite orchestration, the sink-decorator forwards, and the BigQuery overwrite I/O paths.

## Why you never saw a bot comment on the PR

This repo **deliberately doesn't use Codecov as the gate**. Codecov (`codecov/patch`) posts unreliably here — it's not a required check and often never comments at all. Instead the required `Coverage` job runs a repo-local script (`scripts/patch-coverage.py`) that computes changed-line coverage and **writes the full breakdown to the CI log, not a PR comment**. So all the detail you'd expect from a Codecov comment (the 77.95%, the exact uncovered files/lines) was sitting in the job log — which is what I pulled to diagnose this.

## What I fixed

Added targeted tests (verified locally with `cargo llvm-cov` + the same `patch-coverage.py` gate):

════════════════ #494 ════════════════
TITLE: Sink: Elasticsearch `write_mode: overwrite` via alias swap
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
Add `write_mode: overwrite` support to the Elasticsearch sink. It was deliberately excluded from the initial overwrite feature (#492) because Elasticsearch has **no atomic replace of a concrete index** — a delete-then-reindex would risk data loss if the run fails mid-commit, violating the overwrite safety guarantee (a failed/cancelled run must leave the prior destination intact).

## Motivation
Overwrite (full-refresh) landed on the other 6 upsert-capable sinks (postgres, sqlite, mysql, mssql, mongodb, bigquery) in #492 with an atomic begin-stage → commit-swap lifecycle. Elasticsearch is the one holdout; completing it makes the capability uniform across all keyed-write sinks.

## Proposed design
Alias-based swap (the idiomatic ES pattern for atomic index replacement):
- `begin_overwrite`: create a fresh physical index `<index>-<runid>` (copying the target's mappings/settings), write the run into it.
- `commit_overwrite`: atomically move the read alias `<index>` from the old physical index to the new one in a single `POST _aliases` actions call (ES guarantees atomicity of alias actions), then delete the old physical index.
- `abort_overwrite`: delete the staging physical index; the alias is untouched.
- Requires the configured `index` to be (or become) an **alias**, not a concrete index — document this precondition and detect/validate it. Decide behavior when `index` is currently a concrete index (error with guidance, or one-time convert).

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/elasticsearch/src/sink.rs` (implement the four lifecycle methods + `supported_write_modes` += `Overwrite`), `config.rs` if a precondition/opt-in field is needed.
- `cli/src/registry.rs` (`OVERWRITE_SINK_KINDS` += `"elasticsearch"`).
- Docs: connectors matrix, `docs/book/src/cookbook/upsert.md`, ES README; `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.
- Tests: `crates/sink/elasticsearch/tests/overwrite.rs` (container).

## Acceptance criteria
- ES overwrite atomically swaps via alias; a mid-run failure leaves the previous index/alias intact.
- The `is_subset` schema test + capability-parity test updated; `enum_variant_added` remains a non-issue (`WriteMode` is already `#[non_exhaustive]`).

## References
- #492 (the overwrite feature; ES excluded there with this rationale).
- Analogous inherent-limitation follow-up: #179 (Iceberg overwrite, blocked upstream).

════════════════ #495 ════════════════
TITLE: source-rest: mutual-TLS client-certificate auth
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
Let the `rest` (and `xml`/`graphql`) HTTP sources present a **client certificate + private key** (mutual TLS) on every request, including the auth token request. Configurable from inline PEM, a file path, or a `${secret:…}`/`${vault:…}` reference.

## Motivation
ADP Workforce Now (and other enterprise/gov APIs) require mTLS: the client must present a certificate the server validates. faucet's `reqwest`-based HTTP sources have no client-cert/identity config today, so ADP cannot be replicated at all — it is one of only three hard blockers in the tap-replication audit. Ties to the Primary Goal (be the fastest, most-capable way to move data between endpoints) and Third-Party Connector Friendliness.

## Proposed design
Add an optional `tls` block to the REST source config (and mirror on xml/graphql):
```yaml
source:
  type: rest
  config:
    base_url: "https://api.eu.adp.com"
    tls:
      client_cert: "${secret:adp_cert_pem}"      # PEM (cert chain), inline / file:/ secret
      client_key:  "${secret:adp_key_pem}"       # PEM private key
      # or: client_identity_pkcs12 + password
      min_version: "1.2"                          # optional
```
- Build a `reqwest::Identity` (from PEM pair or PKCS#12) once in `new()` and attach it to the shared `reqwest::Client` (`ClientBuilder::identity`). Requires the `reqwest` `native-tls`/`rustls-tls` identity feature — pick the one already enabled and gate behind a `mtls` crate feature if it pulls new deps.
- The identity must apply to **all** requests the source makes (data + any token-endpoint call). If the token is obtained via a shared `auth:` provider, the provider's HTTP client also needs the identity — decide whether mTLS lives on the source's client only (ADP applies the cert to both the token and data requests, so the provider path matters).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/config.rs` (+ `stream.rs` client build), `crates/source/xml`, `crates/source/graphql`; possibly `crates/auth` if the token request must also present the cert; `crates/core` re-exports if a shared TLS config type is introduced.

## Edge cases
Encrypted private keys (passphrase); PKCS#12 vs PEM; cert chain vs leaf; `verify_ssl:false` self-signed servers (see the separate flag); secret redaction of key material in logs/errors.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source configured with a client cert/key completes a request against an mTLS-requiring endpoint (integration test via a wiremock/rustls server requiring client auth).
- Key material is never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the config/build path.
- Docs + README updated.

## Out of scope
Server-cert pinning; per-request rotating certs.

## References
Meltano tap replication audit; tap-adp (`cert=(pub,priv)` on token + data requests). Blocks: **adp**. Related sink work: #492.

════════════════ #496 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth: OAuth1 (HMAC-SHA256) request-signing provider
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
Add an OAuth1 (one-legged, HMAC-SHA256) auth provider to `faucet-auth`, signing **each request** with consumer key/secret + token key/secret + realm, generating a per-request nonce/timestamp and the OAuth1 `Authorization` header.

## Motivation
NetSuite Token-Based Auth (TBA) is OAuth1 with HMAC-SHA256 — every SuiteQL/REST request carries a signature over the request method+URL+params. faucet-auth today only issues OAuth2 bearer tokens (`static`/`oauth2`/`oauth2_refresh`/`token_endpoint`), which model a *token* applied as a header, not **per-request signing**. So NetSuite cannot be replicated — one of three hard blockers in the tap audit. This is distinct from the `token_endpoint` provider: there is no token to fetch; the credential is computed fresh per request from the URL+method.

## Proposed design
The current `AuthProvider` returns a `Credential` once per token lifetime — OAuth1 needs to sign per request, so this needs a request-signing hook, not just a credential fetch. Options:
1. A new `RequestSigner` capability the HTTP sources call with `(method, url, query)` to produce the `Authorization` header — added as a defaulted trait method / optional provider capability so existing providers are unaffected.
2. Provider config:
```yaml
auth:
  netsuite:
    type: oauth1
    config:
      signature_method: HMAC-SHA256
      consumer_key: "${secret:ns_consumer_key}"
      consumer_secret: "${secret:ns_consumer_secret}"
      token: "${secret:ns_token_key}"
      token_secret: "${secret:ns_token_secret}"
      realm: "${param.account_upper}"   # NetSuite account, uppercased, - -> _
```
Reuse a maintained crate for the signature base string + HMAC (e.g. `oauth1-request` / hand-rolled HMAC-SHA256 over the RFC 5849 base string). NetSuite specifics: HMAC-**SHA256** (not the SHA1 default), realm case-sensitivity, POST body params (SuiteQL) excluded from the signature base as NetSuite expects.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/` (new `oauth1.rs` + `build_provider` arm), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` / `traits.rs` (per-request signing hook, defaulted), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (invoke the signer per request), `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (register the type).

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source with an `oauth1` provider produces a valid RFC 5849 HMAC-SHA256 `Authorization` header verified by a test double; signature stable for fixed nonce/timestamp (unit-tested pure signer).
- Secrets never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the pure signing path.
- Docs + README.

## Out of scope
Three-legged OAuth1 (request/authorize/access token dance); RSA-SHA1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-netsuite uses `requests_oauthlib.OAuth1Session` + `SIGNATURE_HMAC_SHA256`. Blocks: **netsuite** (SuiteQL). NetSuite also self-loads to BigQuery — replaced by native `write_mode` (#492), tracked separately if needed.

════════════════ #497 ════════════════
TITLE: File source: fetch + parse CSV/Excel from an authenticated HTTP/Graph URL
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
A way to **download a file (CSV/Excel) from an authenticated HTTP endpoint** (e.g. Microsoft Graph `/drive/items/{id}/content`) and parse it into records — either by extending `source-csv`/`source-parquet` to accept an authed remote URL, or a small dedicated Graph/HTTP file source.

## Motivation
OneDrive (and SharePoint "files mode") are **not** JSON record APIs — the tap authenticates to Microsoft Graph, downloads an .xlsx/.csv **blob**, and parses it (`openpyxl`/`csv.DictReader`) with header/timeseries handling. The `rest` source reads JSON responses; it cannot fetch a binary and run a CSV/Excel reader over it. So OneDrive is unreplicable — the third hard blocker in the tap audit. faucet already parses CSV/Parquet from local + S3/GCS; the missing piece is fetching the blob over an authed HTTP/Graph URL.

## Proposed design
Preferred: extend the existing file sources with a remote fetch:
```yaml
source:
  type: csv           # (or a new `http-file`)
  config:
    url: "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{id}/items/{item}/content"
    auth: { ref: graph_onedrive }     # reuse faucet-auth (oauth2_refresh)
    format: excel                     # csv | excel
    # sheet, header_row, delimiter, glob-over-a-listing-endpoint, etc.
```
- Reuse `oauth2_refresh` for the Graph token (with rotation persistence, tracked separately).
- Excel parsing needs a reader crate (`calamine` is the standard Rust .xlsx/.xls reader) behind a feature flag.
- Support a listing step (Graph folder search) → one record-stream per matched file, or pair with `matrix` for known file ids.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/csv/` (remote fetch + optional excel via `calamine`), or a new `crates/source/http-file/`; `faucet-auth` reuse; docs + capability matrix; CI `feature-check` matrix if a new feature/crate is added.

## Edge cases
Large files (stream/range download); header detection; Excel multi-sheet + type coercion; Graph download-URL redirects (`@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl`); refresh-token rotation (see linked issue).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fetch + parse a CSV and an XLSX from an authed URL (wiremock serving fixture bytes) into the expected records.
- ≥90% patch coverage on the pure parse path; docs + README.

## Out of scope
Arbitrary binary formats beyond CSV/Excel; write-back to the file store.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-sharepointsites onedrive mode (Graph `/content` + `openpyxl`/`csv`). Blocks: **onedrive** (+ SharePoint files). Depends on refresh-token rotation persistence.

════════════════ #498 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth token_endpoint: custom output header (cookie) + form-encoded body / resource param
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
Extend the existing `token_endpoint` auth provider so the fetched token can be placed in **any header** (not only `Authorization: Bearer`) and so the token request can be **form-encoded** and carry extra params (e.g. `resource=`). The provider already POSTs to an arbitrary endpoint and extracts the token via `token_path`; this is the last mile.

## Motivation
Two taps need auth flows that are *almost* covered today:
- **SAP Business One** (`tap-sap`): `POST /b1s/v1/Login {CompanyDB,UserName,Password}` returns a `SessionId` that must be carried as **`Cookie: B1SESSION=<id>; CompanyDB=<db>`** on every request — not an `Authorization` header. `token_endpoint` already fetches the id (`token_path: $.SessionId`), and `faucet_core::auth::Credential::Header { name, value }` **already** exists and the REST source already applies it as an arbitrary header. The provider just hardcodes `Credential::Bearer`.
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): Azure AD **v1** `/oauth2/token` with a **form-encoded** body containing `resource=https://{host}`. `oauth2` sends `scope` not `resource`; `token_endpoint` currently posts **JSON** (`req.json(body)`), which the OAuth token endpoint rejects.

Both reduce to small, additive knobs on `token_endpoint`. This is what reclassified SAP from "blocked" to "small enhancement" in the tap-replication audit.

## Proposed design
Add optional config to `token_endpoint` (`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs`):
```yaml
auth:
  sap:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${param.pass}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as:                                    # NEW; default = Authorization: Bearer {token}
        header: "Cookie"
        template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}"
  fno:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/token"
      encoding: form                               # NEW; default = json
      body: { grant_type: client_credentials, client_id: "…", client_secret: "…", resource: "https://${param.subdomain}.operations.dynamics.com" }
      token_path: "$.access_token"
```
- `apply_as` → return `Credential::Header { name, value }` (already applied by `rest`) with `{token}` substituted; default keeps `Credential::Bearer`.
- `encoding: form|json` → `req.form(body)` vs `req.json(body)`.
- Optional: re-auth on a 401 (SAP sessions expire ~30 min; the tap has no re-login — faucet can be better here).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs` (config + apply + encoding), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` (already has `Credential::Header`), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (already maps `Credential::Header` → `Auth::Custom`; verify multi-header/cookie value passes through), docs.


════════════════ #499 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth oauth2_refresh: persist the rotated refresh_token to the state store
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
When an OAuth2 provider (e.g. Microsoft, Rippling) **rotates the refresh_token** on each refresh, `oauth2_refresh` must persist the new refresh_token durably so the *next* run authenticates. Today rotation is handled in-memory only, so a second scheduled run 401s.

## Motivation
- **Rippling** (`tap-rippling`): rotates the refresh_token on every refresh; the tap writes the new one to `/tmp/refresh_token.txt` for the next ECS run. A faucet `oauth2_refresh` provider that rotates in-memory works for one run but the next run presents the now-invalidated original → 401.
- **OneDrive** (`tap-sharepointsites` onedrive mode): same — Microsoft rotates the refresh_token each use.

This is a reliability gap: single-run replicas pass, scheduled/repeated runs fail. Ties to the Primary Goal (reliability).

## Proposed design
- Give `oauth2_refresh` an optional durable store hook so it can write the rotated `refresh_token` (and expiry) back. Reuse the pipeline's `StateStore` (the same durable backend used for bookmarks) under a dedicated key, e.g. `auth:oauth2_refresh:<provider-name>`.
- On startup, read the stored refresh_token (if present) in preference to the config's seed value; on each rotation, atomically persist the new one.
- Must be safe across concurrent rows sharing one provider (single-flight already exists) and across process restarts.
- Config: opt-in `persist: true` (or automatic when a state store is configured), referencing the run's state backend.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/oauth2.rs` (`OAuth2RefreshProvider`), a bridge to `faucet_core::StateStore`, `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (wire the state backend into provider construction), docs.

## Edge cases
Provider shared by N matrix rows (persist once, single-flight); first run with only a seed token; store unavailable (fail closed vs warn); secret redaction of the persisted token.

## Acceptance criteria
- A simulated rotating token endpoint: run 1 rotates + persists; run 2 (fresh process/provider) reads the persisted token and authenticates (integration test with a wiremock rotating endpoint + a file/memory state store).
- Token never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the persistence path.

## Out of scope
Non-rotating providers (unaffected); OAuth1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-rippling `REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE`, tap-sharepointsites onedrive rotation. Unblocks: **rippling, onedrive**.

════════════════ #500 ════════════════
TITLE: source-rest: POST-search pagination (cursor + filter in the request body)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
Add a REST pagination style for **POST search** endpoints where the next-page cursor (and the incremental filter) live **in the request JSON body**, not in a query param or a next-link. The paginator must inject the extracted cursor back into the body for the next request.

## Motivation
- **HubSpot CRM** (`tap-hubspot`): reads objects via `POST /crm/v3/objects/{obj}/search` with a JSON body `{filterGroups, limit, sorts, properties, after}`; the next cursor is `$.paging.next.after` and is placed back into `payload.after`. The incremental filter (`hs_lastmodifieddate GTE …`) is also in the body. faucet's `rest` source supports POST + body, but its pagination styles (Cursor/PageNumber/Offset/LinkHeader/NextLinkInBody) all advance a **query param or next-link**, not a body field.
- **NetSuite SuiteQL** (`tap-netsuite`) posts `{"q":"SELECT …"}` with offset/limit — a related body-driven pattern (though offset there is a URL param).

Without this, HubSpot's core object streams can't paginate faithfully.

## Proposed design
A new `PaginationStyle::CursorInBody` (name TBD) on the REST source:
```yaml
pagination:
  type: CursorInBody
  next_token_path: "$.paging.next.after"     # where the next cursor is read from the response
  body_cursor_field: "after"                 # where to write it into the next request body
  # stops when next_token_path is null/absent; loop-guard on repeated token (as Cursor does)
```
- Reuse the existing cursor loop-detection + `max_pages` cap.
- The initial body comes from `source.config.body`; each subsequent request sets `body[body_cursor_field] = <extracted cursor>`.
- Consider a companion for HubSpot's 10k-result `hs_object_id GT <last>` re-filter (a secondary body mutation when a page count threshold is hit) — could be a follow-up.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/pagination/` (new module + `PaginationStyle` variant + `advance` handling that mutates the body), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (thread the body mutation into the next request), docs (pagination table in `.claude/rules/connectors.md` + the docs site).

## Acceptance criteria
- A wiremock POST-search endpoint returning `paging.next.after` paginates to completion, injecting the cursor into the body each page; loop guard + `max_pages` honored. Unit + integration tests.
- ≥90% patch coverage.

## Out of scope
GraphQL (has its own source); the HubSpot 10k re-filter (separate follow-up); dynamic property discovery (separate).

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-hubspot object search. Unblocks: **hubspot** (core objects); related: **netsuite** SuiteQL. Pagination styles: `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.

════════════════ #501 ════════════════
TITLE: CLI: discovery-driven request matrix (fan out over dimensions fetched at plan time)
LABELS: feature,tier-3
## Summary
Let a matrix fan out over a **dimension set discovered at plan time from another endpoint/query**, not just a static list. i.e. "run this stream once per {company / subsidiary / custom-field / list-id} returned by a discovery call."

## Motivation
Several taps compute their request set from a *live* enumeration before syncing:
- **Rillet report streams** (`tap-rillet`): month windows **×** subsidiary ids **×** custom-field ids, where the id lists are fetched from `/subsidiaries`, `/fields`, and a `/reports/balance-sheet?breakdown_by=SUBSIDIARY` probe at plan time.
- **Dynamics 365 BC** (`tap-dynamics-business-central`): `GET /companies` then every entity is fanned out per company × environment.
- **BambooHR** custom reports, **HubSpot** child associations — similar "enumerate then fan out" shapes.

faucet's `matrix` supports static rows and parent→child fan-out over *records the parent stream emitted*, but not "fan out over the distinct values of a discovery query/endpoint" as a first-class, cached, plan-time step. This is the single biggest structural gap for report-style taps.

## Proposed design (sketch — needs design discussion)
A matrix row (or a new pre-step) that declares a discovery source and a projection:
```yaml
matrix:
  - id: subsidiaries          # discovery step
    discover:
      source: { type: rest, config: { path: "/subsidiaries", records_path: "$.subsidiaries[*]" } }
      as: subsidiary_id
      select: "$.id"
  - id: trial_balance
    for_each: subsidiaries    # one invocation per discovered subsidiary_id
    source: { config: { path: "/reports/trial-balance", query_params: { subsidiary_id: "${subsidiaries.subsidiary_id}" } } }
```
- Discovery runs once, results cached; the dependent rows expand to N invocations (compose with the existing `${now.*}` / backfill month windows for the cross-product).
- Overlaps with `faucet discover` (#211) and the parent/child matrix — evaluate whether this is a new matrix mode or an extension of `parent:`.

## Affected crates / files
`cli/src/expand.rs` / `executor.rs` (plan-time discovery + fan-out), `cli/src/config.rs` (grammar), docs. Likely reuses `Source::discover` where a catalog exists, else a generic "distinct values of a query" step.

## Acceptance criteria
- A config that fans a stream out over the ids returned by a discovery call produces N invocations, cached once; composes with `matrix` date windows. Tests on the pure planning logic.

## Out of scope (v1)
The deep report-tree flattening that follows (that's a transform, tracked separately); recursion.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-rillet report fan-out, tap-dynamics-business-central company enumeration. Related: #211 (discover), matrix parent/child. Partial for: **rillet reports, ms365bc**.

TITLE: source: completeness reconciliation (rows fetched vs authoritative count)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
An opt-in guard that compares the number of rows a source actually fetched against an **authoritative count** for the same filter, and fails the run on a shortfall beyond a tolerance — catching silent truncation (a half-read table quietly overwriting a full one).

## Motivation
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): after each stream it issues OData `$count=true&$top=0`, reads `@odata.count`, and compares against the distinct-PK count fetched; a shortfall beyond `source_count_recon_tolerance_pct` raises `SilentTruncationError` and fails the tap. This exists specifically because offset/skip paging can silently truncate a full-refresh — exactly the scenario `write_mode: overwrite` (#492) makes dangerous (a truncated read would replace good data with less).

faucet has SLA `min_rows_per_run` (#202) and volume anomaly detection, which partially cover the intent, but not a per-run *authoritative count* comparison for a specific source.

## Proposed design
- A source-level (or pipeline-level) `reconcile:` option: after the run, fetch a count via a configured probe (OData `$count`, a SQL `SELECT count(*)`, etc.) over the same filter, compare to rows emitted, and fail if `fetched < count * (1 - tolerance)`.
- Compose with `write_mode: overwrite` so an overwrite never truncates on a short read.
- For sources without a native count, this is a no-op / not offered.

## Affected crates / files
Likely a CLI-layer post-run check (like SLA in `cli/src/sla/`) that can issue a count probe, or a `Source` capability method `estimated/exact count`. Reuse `faucet_core::discover::estimated_rows` where present. Docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- A source that under-reads (simulated) fails the run when reconcile is on and the shortfall exceeds tolerance; passes within tolerance. Pure comparison logic unit-tested.

## Out of scope
Per-partition recon internals (F&O also reconciles each key-range — a follow-up); sources with no count.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-dynamics-finance `$count` recon + `SilentTruncationError`. Related: SLA #202, overwrite #492. Strengthens: all overwrite/full-refresh runs; directly: **ms365fno**.

TITLE: source-rest: stop pagination on HTTP 204 No Content
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
Add `204 No Content` as a pagination stop condition for the REST source's offset/skip paginator.

## Motivation
- **ADP** (`tap-adp`): paginates with OData `$top`/`$skip` and stops when the server returns **`204 No Content`** (rather than an empty JSON array). faucet's offset paginator stops on a zero-record page / offset≥total, not on a 204 status.

════════════════ #494 ════════════════
TITLE: Sink: Elasticsearch `write_mode: overwrite` via alias swap
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
Add `write_mode: overwrite` support to the Elasticsearch sink. It was deliberately excluded from the initial overwrite feature (#492) because Elasticsearch has **no atomic replace of a concrete index** — a delete-then-reindex would risk data loss if the run fails mid-commit, violating the overwrite safety guarantee (a failed/cancelled run must leave the prior destination intact).

## Motivation
Overwrite (full-refresh) landed on the other 6 upsert-capable sinks (postgres, sqlite, mysql, mssql, mongodb, bigquery) in #492 with an atomic begin-stage → commit-swap lifecycle. Elasticsearch is the one holdout; completing it makes the capability uniform across all keyed-write sinks.

## Proposed design
Alias-based swap (the idiomatic ES pattern for atomic index replacement):
- `begin_overwrite`: create a fresh physical index `<index>-<runid>` (copying the target's mappings/settings), write the run into it.
- `commit_overwrite`: atomically move the read alias `<index>` from the old physical index to the new one in a single `POST _aliases` actions call (ES guarantees atomicity of alias actions), then delete the old physical index.
- `abort_overwrite`: delete the staging physical index; the alias is untouched.
- Requires the configured `index` to be (or become) an **alias**, not a concrete index — document this precondition and detect/validate it. Decide behavior when `index` is currently a concrete index (error with guidance, or one-time convert).

## Affected crates / files
- `crates/sink/elasticsearch/src/sink.rs` (implement the four lifecycle methods + `supported_write_modes` += `Overwrite`), `config.rs` if a precondition/opt-in field is needed.
- `cli/src/registry.rs` (`OVERWRITE_SINK_KINDS` += `"elasticsearch"`).
- Docs: connectors matrix, `docs/book/src/cookbook/upsert.md`, ES README; `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.
- Tests: `crates/sink/elasticsearch/tests/overwrite.rs` (container).

## Acceptance criteria
- ES overwrite atomically swaps via alias; a mid-run failure leaves the previous index/alias intact.
- The `is_subset` schema test + capability-parity test updated; `enum_variant_added` remains a non-issue (`WriteMode` is already `#[non_exhaustive]`).

## References
- #492 (the overwrite feature; ES excluded there with this rationale).
- Analogous inherent-limitation follow-up: #179 (Iceberg overwrite, blocked upstream).

════════════════ #495 ════════════════
TITLE: source-rest: mutual-TLS client-certificate auth
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
Let the `rest` (and `xml`/`graphql`) HTTP sources present a **client certificate + private key** (mutual TLS) on every request, including the auth token request. Configurable from inline PEM, a file path, or a `${secret:…}`/`${vault:…}` reference.

## Motivation
ADP Workforce Now (and other enterprise/gov APIs) require mTLS: the client must present a certificate the server validates. faucet's `reqwest`-based HTTP sources have no client-cert/identity config today, so ADP cannot be replicated at all — it is one of only three hard blockers in the tap-replication audit. Ties to the Primary Goal (be the fastest, most-capable way to move data between endpoints) and Third-Party Connector Friendliness.

## Proposed design
Add an optional `tls` block to the REST source config (and mirror on xml/graphql):
```yaml
source:
  type: rest
  config:
    base_url: "https://api.eu.adp.com"
    tls:
      client_cert: "${secret:adp_cert_pem}"      # PEM (cert chain), inline / file:/ secret
      client_key:  "${secret:adp_key_pem}"       # PEM private key
      # or: client_identity_pkcs12 + password
      min_version: "1.2"                          # optional
```
- Build a `reqwest::Identity` (from PEM pair or PKCS#12) once in `new()` and attach it to the shared `reqwest::Client` (`ClientBuilder::identity`). Requires the `reqwest` `native-tls`/`rustls-tls` identity feature — pick the one already enabled and gate behind a `mtls` crate feature if it pulls new deps.
- The identity must apply to **all** requests the source makes (data + any token-endpoint call). If the token is obtained via a shared `auth:` provider, the provider's HTTP client also needs the identity — decide whether mTLS lives on the source's client only (ADP applies the cert to both the token and data requests, so the provider path matters).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/config.rs` (+ `stream.rs` client build), `crates/source/xml`, `crates/source/graphql`; possibly `crates/auth` if the token request must also present the cert; `crates/core` re-exports if a shared TLS config type is introduced.

## Edge cases
Encrypted private keys (passphrase); PKCS#12 vs PEM; cert chain vs leaf; `verify_ssl:false` self-signed servers (see the separate flag); secret redaction of key material in logs/errors.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source configured with a client cert/key completes a request against an mTLS-requiring endpoint (integration test via a wiremock/rustls server requiring client auth).
- Key material is never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the config/build path.
- Docs + README updated.

## Out of scope
Server-cert pinning; per-request rotating certs.

## References
Meltano tap replication audit; tap-adp (`cert=(pub,priv)` on token + data requests). Blocks: **adp**. Related sink work: #492.

════════════════ #496 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth: OAuth1 (HMAC-SHA256) request-signing provider
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
Add an OAuth1 (one-legged, HMAC-SHA256) auth provider to `faucet-auth`, signing **each request** with consumer key/secret + token key/secret + realm, generating a per-request nonce/timestamp and the OAuth1 `Authorization` header.

## Motivation
NetSuite Token-Based Auth (TBA) is OAuth1 with HMAC-SHA256 — every SuiteQL/REST request carries a signature over the request method+URL+params. faucet-auth today only issues OAuth2 bearer tokens (`static`/`oauth2`/`oauth2_refresh`/`token_endpoint`), which model a *token* applied as a header, not **per-request signing**. So NetSuite cannot be replicated — one of three hard blockers in the tap audit. This is distinct from the `token_endpoint` provider: there is no token to fetch; the credential is computed fresh per request from the URL+method.

## Proposed design
The current `AuthProvider` returns a `Credential` once per token lifetime — OAuth1 needs to sign per request, so this needs a request-signing hook, not just a credential fetch. Options:
1. A new `RequestSigner` capability the HTTP sources call with `(method, url, query)` to produce the `Authorization` header — added as a defaulted trait method / optional provider capability so existing providers are unaffected.
2. Provider config:
```yaml
auth:
  netsuite:
    type: oauth1
    config:
      signature_method: HMAC-SHA256
      consumer_key: "${secret:ns_consumer_key}"
      consumer_secret: "${secret:ns_consumer_secret}"
      token: "${secret:ns_token_key}"
      token_secret: "${secret:ns_token_secret}"
      realm: "${param.account_upper}"   # NetSuite account, uppercased, - -> _
```
Reuse a maintained crate for the signature base string + HMAC (e.g. `oauth1-request` / hand-rolled HMAC-SHA256 over the RFC 5849 base string). NetSuite specifics: HMAC-**SHA256** (not the SHA1 default), realm case-sensitivity, POST body params (SuiteQL) excluded from the signature base as NetSuite expects.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/` (new `oauth1.rs` + `build_provider` arm), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` / `traits.rs` (per-request signing hook, defaulted), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (invoke the signer per request), `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (register the type).

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rest` source with an `oauth1` provider produces a valid RFC 5849 HMAC-SHA256 `Authorization` header verified by a test double; signature stable for fixed nonce/timestamp (unit-tested pure signer).
- Secrets never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the pure signing path.
- Docs + README.

## Out of scope
Three-legged OAuth1 (request/authorize/access token dance); RSA-SHA1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-netsuite uses `requests_oauthlib.OAuth1Session` + `SIGNATURE_HMAC_SHA256`. Blocks: **netsuite** (SuiteQL). NetSuite also self-loads to BigQuery — replaced by native `write_mode` (#492), tracked separately if needed.

TITLE: File source: fetch + parse CSV/Excel from an authenticated HTTP/Graph URL
LABELS: feature,tier-2
## Summary
A way to **download a file (CSV/Excel) from an authenticated HTTP endpoint** (e.g. Microsoft Graph `/drive/items/{id}/content`) and parse it into records — either by extending `source-csv`/`source-parquet` to accept an authed remote URL, or a small dedicated Graph/HTTP file source.

OneDrive (and SharePoint "files mode") are **not** JSON record APIs — the tap authenticates to Microsoft Graph, downloads an .xlsx/.csv **blob**, and parses it (`openpyxl`/`csv.DictReader`) with header/timeseries handling. Preferred: extend the existing file sources with a remote fetch:
```yaml
source:
  type: csv           # (or a new `http-file`)
  config:
    url: "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{id}/items/{item}/content"
    auth: { ref: graph_onedrive }     # reuse faucet-auth (oauth2_refresh)
```

`crates/source/csv/` (remote fetch + optional excel via `calamine`), or a new `crates/source/http-file/`; `faucet-auth` reuse; docs + capability matrix; CI `feature-check` matrix if a new feature/crate is added.

Large files (stream/range download); header detection; Excel multi-sheet + type coercion; Graph download-URL redirects (`@microsoft.graph.downloadUrl`); refresh-token rotation (see linked issue).

## Acceptance criteria
- Fetch + parse a CSV and an XLSX from an authed URL (wiremock serving fixture bytes) into the expected records.
- ≥90% patch coverage on the pure parse path; docs + README.

## Out of scope
Arbitrary binary formats beyond CSV/Excel; write-back to the file store.

Meltano tap audit; tap-sharepointsites onedrive mode (Graph `/content` + `openpyxl`/`csv`). Blocks: **onedrive** (+ SharePoint files). Depends on refresh-token rotation persistence.

════════════════ #498 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth token_endpoint: custom output header (cookie) + form-encoded body / resource param
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
Extend the existing `token_endpoint` auth provider so the fetched token can be placed in **any header** (not only `Authorization: Bearer`) and so the token request can be **form-encoded** and carry extra params (e.g. `resource=`). The provider already POSTs to an arbitrary endpoint and extracts the token via `token_path`; this is the last mile.

## Motivation
Two taps need auth flows that are *almost* covered today:
- **SAP Business One** (`tap-sap`): `POST /b1s/v1/Login {CompanyDB,UserName,Password}` returns a `SessionId` that must be carried as **`Cookie: B1SESSION=<id>; CompanyDB=<db>`** on every request — not an `Authorization` header. `token_endpoint` already fetches the id (`token_path: $.SessionId`), and `faucet_core::auth::Credential::Header { name, value }` **already** exists and the REST source already applies it as an arbitrary header. The provider just hardcodes `Credential::Bearer`.
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): Azure AD **v1** `/oauth2/token` with a **form-encoded** body containing `resource=https://{host}`. `oauth2` sends `scope` not `resource`; `token_endpoint` currently posts **JSON** (`req.json(body)`), which the OAuth token endpoint rejects.

Both reduce to small, additive knobs on `token_endpoint`. This is what reclassified SAP from "blocked" to "small enhancement" in the tap-replication audit.

## Proposed design
Add optional config to `token_endpoint` (`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs`):
```yaml
auth:
  sap:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${param.pass}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as:                                    # NEW; default = Authorization: Bearer {token}
        header: "Cookie"
        template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}"
  fno:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/token"
      encoding: form                               # NEW; default = json
      body: { grant_type: client_credentials, client_id: "…", client_secret: "…", resource: "https://${param.subdomain}.operations.dynamics.com" }
      token_path: "$.access_token"
```
- `apply_as` → return `Credential::Header { name, value }` (already applied by `rest`) with `{token}` substituted; default keeps `Credential::Bearer`.
- `encoding: form|json` → `req.form(body)` vs `req.json(body)`.
- Optional: re-auth on a 401 (SAP sessions expire ~30 min; the tap has no re-login — faucet can be better here).

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/token_endpoint.rs` (config + apply + encoding), `crates/core/src/auth.rs` (already has `Credential::Header`), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (already maps `Credential::Header` → `Auth::Custom`; verify multi-header/cookie value passes through), docs.


════════════════ #499 ════════════════
TITLE: faucet-auth oauth2_refresh: persist the rotated refresh_token to the state store
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
When an OAuth2 provider (e.g. Microsoft, Rippling) **rotates the refresh_token** on each refresh, `oauth2_refresh` must persist the new refresh_token durably so the *next* run authenticates. Today rotation is handled in-memory only, so a second scheduled run 401s.

## Motivation
- **Rippling** (`tap-rippling`): rotates the refresh_token on every refresh; the tap writes the new one to `/tmp/refresh_token.txt` for the next ECS run. A faucet `oauth2_refresh` provider that rotates in-memory works for one run but the next run presents the now-invalidated original → 401.
- **OneDrive** (`tap-sharepointsites` onedrive mode): same — Microsoft rotates the refresh_token each use.

This is a reliability gap: single-run replicas pass, scheduled/repeated runs fail. Ties to the Primary Goal (reliability).

## Proposed design
- Give `oauth2_refresh` an optional durable store hook so it can write the rotated `refresh_token` (and expiry) back. Reuse the pipeline's `StateStore` (the same durable backend used for bookmarks) under a dedicated key, e.g. `auth:oauth2_refresh:<provider-name>`.
- On startup, read the stored refresh_token (if present) in preference to the config's seed value; on each rotation, atomically persist the new one.
- Must be safe across concurrent rows sharing one provider (single-flight already exists) and across process restarts.
- Config: opt-in `persist: true` (or automatic when a state store is configured), referencing the run's state backend.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/auth/src/oauth2.rs` (`OAuth2RefreshProvider`), a bridge to `faucet_core::StateStore`, `cli/src/auth_catalog.rs` (wire the state backend into provider construction), docs.

## Edge cases
Provider shared by N matrix rows (persist once, single-flight); first run with only a seed token; store unavailable (fail closed vs warn); secret redaction of the persisted token.

## Acceptance criteria
- A simulated rotating token endpoint: run 1 rotates + persists; run 2 (fresh process/provider) reads the persisted token and authenticates (integration test with a wiremock rotating endpoint + a file/memory state store).
- Token never logged; ≥90% patch coverage on the persistence path.

## Out of scope
Non-rotating providers (unaffected); OAuth1.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-rippling `REFRESH_TOKEN_FILE`, tap-sharepointsites onedrive rotation. Unblocks: **rippling, onedrive**.

════════════════ #500 ════════════════
TITLE: source-rest: POST-search pagination (cursor + filter in the request body)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-2
## Summary
Add a REST pagination style for **POST search** endpoints where the next-page cursor (and the incremental filter) live **in the request JSON body**, not in a query param or a next-link. The paginator must inject the extracted cursor back into the body for the next request.

## Motivation
- **HubSpot CRM** (`tap-hubspot`): reads objects via `POST /crm/v3/objects/{obj}/search` with a JSON body `{filterGroups, limit, sorts, properties, after}`; the next cursor is `$.paging.next.after` and is placed back into `payload.after`. The incremental filter (`hs_lastmodifieddate GTE …`) is also in the body. faucet's `rest` source supports POST + body, but its pagination styles (Cursor/PageNumber/Offset/LinkHeader/NextLinkInBody) all advance a **query param or next-link**, not a body field.
- **NetSuite SuiteQL** (`tap-netsuite`) posts `{"q":"SELECT …"}` with offset/limit — a related body-driven pattern (though offset there is a URL param).

Without this, HubSpot's core object streams can't paginate faithfully.

## Proposed design
A new `PaginationStyle::CursorInBody` (name TBD) on the REST source:
```yaml
pagination:
  type: CursorInBody
  next_token_path: "$.paging.next.after"     # where the next cursor is read from the response
  body_cursor_field: "after"                 # where to write it into the next request body
  # stops when next_token_path is null/absent; loop-guard on repeated token (as Cursor does)
```
- Reuse the existing cursor loop-detection + `max_pages` cap.
- The initial body comes from `source.config.body`; each subsequent request sets `body[body_cursor_field] = <extracted cursor>`.
- Consider a companion for HubSpot's 10k-result `hs_object_id GT <last>` re-filter (a secondary body mutation when a page count threshold is hit) — could be a follow-up.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/pagination/` (new module + `PaginationStyle` variant + `advance` handling that mutates the body), `crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (thread the body mutation into the next request), docs (pagination table in `.claude/rules/connectors.md` + the docs site).

## Acceptance criteria
- A wiremock POST-search endpoint returning `paging.next.after` paginates to completion, injecting the cursor into the body each page; loop guard + `max_pages` honored. Unit + integration tests.
- ≥90% patch coverage.

## Out of scope
GraphQL (has its own source); the HubSpot 10k re-filter (separate follow-up); dynamic property discovery (separate).

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-hubspot object search. Unblocks: **hubspot** (core objects); related: **netsuite** SuiteQL. Pagination styles: `.claude/rules/connectors.md`.

TITLE: source: completeness reconciliation (rows fetched vs authoritative count)
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
An opt-in guard that compares the number of rows a source actually fetched against an **authoritative count** for the same filter, and fails the run on a shortfall beyond a tolerance — catching silent truncation (a half-read table quietly overwriting a full one).

## Motivation
- **Dynamics 365 F&O** (`tap-dynamics-finance`): after each stream it issues OData `$count=true&$top=0`, reads `@odata.count`, and compares against the distinct-PK count fetched; a shortfall beyond `source_count_recon_tolerance_pct` raises `SilentTruncationError` and fails the tap. This exists specifically because offset/skip paging can silently truncate a full-refresh — exactly the scenario `write_mode: overwrite` (#492) makes dangerous (a truncated read would replace good data with less).

faucet has SLA `min_rows_per_run` (#202) and volume anomaly detection, which partially cover the intent, but not a per-run *authoritative count* comparison for a specific source.

## Proposed design
- A source-level (or pipeline-level) `reconcile:` option: after the run, fetch a count via a configured probe (OData `$count`, a SQL `SELECT count(*)`, etc.) over the same filter, compare to rows emitted, and fail if `fetched < count * (1 - tolerance)`.
- Compose with `write_mode: overwrite` so an overwrite never truncates on a short read.
- For sources without a native count, this is a no-op / not offered.

## Affected crates / files
Likely a CLI-layer post-run check (like SLA in `cli/src/sla/`) that can issue a count probe, or a `Source` capability method `estimated/exact count`. Reuse `faucet_core::discover::estimated_rows` where present. Docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- A source that under-reads (simulated) fails the run when reconcile is on and the shortfall exceeds tolerance; passes within tolerance. Pure comparison logic unit-tested.

## Out of scope
Per-partition recon internals (F&O also reconciles each key-range — a follow-up); sources with no count.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-dynamics-finance `$count` recon + `SilentTruncationError`. Related: SLA #202, overwrite #492. Strengthens: all overwrite/full-refresh runs; directly: **ms365fno**.

TITLE: source-rest: stop pagination on HTTP 204 No Content
LABELS: enhancement,tier-3
## Summary
Add `204 No Content` as a pagination stop condition for the REST source's offset/skip paginator.

## Motivation
- **ADP** (`tap-adp`): paginates with OData `$top`/`$skip` and stops when the server returns **`204 No Content`** (rather than an empty JSON array). faucet's offset paginator stops on a zero-record page / offset≥total, not on a 204 status.

Minor, but it's the difference between a faithful ADP replica and an extra empty request or a hang.

## Proposed design
- In the REST source's pagination loop, treat a `204` response (empty body) as a terminal "no more pages" signal for the offset/page styles (and arguably all styles). Guard so a 204 mid-stream ends cleanly rather than erroring on empty-body JSON parse.

## Affected crates / files
`crates/source/rest/src/stream.rs` (response handling) + `pagination/` stop conditions; docs (pagination table).

## Acceptance criteria
- A wiremock endpoint returning rows then a `204` terminates pagination without error and without an extra empty page. Unit/integration test.

## Out of scope
Non-204 empty-signal conventions.

## References
Meltano tap audit; tap-adp `ADPPaginator` stops on 204. Part of the ADP replica (mTLS is the hard blocker, see the mTLS issue).

A cached token that the API later rejects with **401 Unauthorized** (a server-side expiry the time-based cache can't see, including the cached-indefinitely case) is invalidated and the request is retried once with a freshly-fetched token, so a long run doesn't abort mid-way.

| Style | Stops When |

file.content:
## Pagination

The `pagination` field selects a `PaginationStyle` (tagged by `type`). `max_pages` is a hard cap across all styles.

| Style (`type`) | Fields | Stops when |
|----------------|--------|------------|
| `None` | — | After the first page. |
| `Cursor` | `next_token_path`, `param_name` | Next-token JSONPath is null/absent, or the same cursor repeats (loop detection). |
| `LinkHeader` | — | No `rel="next"` in the `Link` response header, or the same link repeats. |
| `NextLinkInBody` | `next_link_path` | Next-page URL is absent, null, empty, or repeats. |
| `PageNumber` | `param_name`, `start_page`, `page_size`, `page_size_param` | A zero-record page, or the same body returned twice in a row (content-stagnation detection for APIs that clamp out-of-range pages). |
| `Offset` | `offset_param`, `limit_param`, `limit`, `total_path` | A zero-record page, offset reaches `total` (via `total_path`), or a page returns fewer records than `limit`. |

## Streaming & batching

`RestStream` overrides `Source::stream_pages`, fetching the next HTTP page on demand and yielding it as a `StreamPage`. `Pipeline::run` writes each page to the sink as it arrives, so peak memory is bounded at one page no matter how large the feed. The bookmark is carried on the final page (incremental mode) so the state store advances only after the sink confirms the full run.

The inherent `stream_pages()` method (yielding `Vec<Value>` pages, no per-page bookmark) remains for direct callers, alongside the eager `fetch_all()` / `fetch_all_incremental()` helpers.

The bookmark is carried on the final page (incremental mode) so the state store advances only after the sink confirms the full run.

input.new_string:
| `refresh_token` | string | — *(required)* | Initial (seed) refresh token. A rotated token in the response is captured in place for the next refresh. |
| `expiry_ratio` | number | `0.9` | Refresh after `expires_in × expiry_ratio` seconds. Must be a finite number in `(0, 1]`. |
| `persist` | object | *(none)* | Durably persist the rotated `refresh_token` so a **later** run authenticates after the token rotates (providers like Microsoft / Rippling rotate on every refresh; without this the second scheduled run 401s). `persist.path` is a file-backed state-store directory; the rotated token is written after each refresh and re-read on startup in preference to the config seed. Optional `persist.key` overrides the auto-derived (stable, identity-scoped) storage key. |

`persist` example:

```yaml
auth:
  graph:
    type: oauth2_refresh
    config:
      token_url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token"
      client_id: "${secret:graph_client_id}"
      client_secret: "${secret:graph_client_secret}"
      refresh_token: "${secret:graph_seed_refresh_token}"   # seed; used only until the first rotation
      persist:
        path: "./state/auth"        # rotated refresh_token survives across runs
```

### `token_endpoint`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `url` | string | — *(required)* | HTTP endpoint to fetch the token from. |
| `method` | string | `POST` | HTTP method. |
| `encoding` | string | `json` | Request-body encoding: `json` (default) or `form` (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, required by OAuth token endpoints that expect a `resource=` param). `form` requires a flat object `body` of string/number/boolean values. |
| `body` | object | *(none)* | Request body (e.g. carrying `client_id` / `client_secret` / `resource`). Omit for a GET. |
| `token_path` | string | — *(required)* | JSONPath selecting the token from the response (e.g. `$.auth.access_token`). String and numeric matches are accepted. |
| `expiry_path` | string | *(none)* | JSONPath selecting `expires_in` (seconds) from the response. When absent, the token is cached without an expiry. |
| `expiry_ratio` | number | `0.9` | Refresh after `expires_in × expiry_ratio` seconds. Must be a finite number in `(0, 1]`. |
| `apply_as` | object | *(Bearer)* | Where the fetched token is placed on each request. Default is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Set `apply_as: { header, template }` to place it in an arbitrary header (e.g. a session cookie): `template` is the header value with `{token}` substituted (defaults to the bare token). |

`apply_as` example — SAP Business One session cookie:

```yaml
auth:
  sap:
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${secret:sap_pw}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as:
        header: "Cookie"
        template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}"
```

# Pagination styles (REST source)

The REST source walks multi-page responses automatically. Set `pagination.type`
to one of the styles below. `max_pages` is a hard cap across all of them, and
every style has a loop/termination guard so a misbehaving API can't loop forever.

| Style | Stops when |
|-------|-----------|
| `None` | after the first page |
| `Cursor` | the next-token JSONPath is null/absent (or repeats) |
| `PageNumber` | a page returns zero records (or an identical body repeats) |
| `Offset` | the offset reaches `total` (via `total_path`) or a short page arrives |
| `LinkHeader` | there's no `rel="next"` in the `Link` response header |
| `NextLinkInBody` | the next-page URL in the body is absent, null, or empty |

## Cursor

```yaml
pagination:
  type: Cursor
  next_token_path: $.meta.next_cursor  # JSONPath to the next-page token
  param_name: starting_after           # query param to send it back as
```

## Page number

```yaml
pagination:
  type: PageNumber
  param_name: page
  start_page: 1
  page_size: 500
  page_size_param: per_page
```

## Offset / limit

```yaml
pagination:
  type: Offset
  limit: 1000
  limit_param: limit
  offset_param: offset
  total_path: $.meta.total             # optional; enables an exact stop
```

## Link header

```yaml
pagination:
  type: LinkHeader      # follows the RFC 5988 `Link: <…>; rel="next"` header
```

## Next link in body

```yaml
pagination:
  type: NextLinkInBody
  next_link_path: $.links.next         # JSONPath to the absolute next-page URL
```

> Use `faucet schema source rest` to see the exact fields and defaults for each
> style in your installed version.

## Custom token endpoint

For non-standard token endpoints, `token_endpoint` lets you describe the request
and point at the access-token and expiry fields in the response. See
`faucet schema source rest` for the full field list.

## Shared auth providers (`auth: { ref }`)

When several connectors authenticate against the **same** system — e.g. four
matrix rows reading four endpoints of one API, or four Snowflake tables — define
the credential **once** in the top-level `auth:` catalog and reference it with
`auth: { ref: <name> }`. faucet builds a single provider and shares it across
every row, so there is **one** token fetch and **one** refresh cycle
(single-flight) instead of each row racing to refresh a single-active / rotating
token:

```yaml
auth:
  api:
    type: oauth2_refresh        # rotating refresh token captured centrally
    config:
      token_url: ${env:API_TOKEN_URL}
      client_id: ${secret:API_CLIENT_ID}
      client_secret: ${secret:API_CLIENT_SECRET}
      refresh_token: ${secret:API_REFRESH_TOKEN}
pipeline:
  sources:
    ep:
      type: rest
      config:
        base_url: ${env:API_BASE_URL}
        auth: { ref: api }      # every row sharing this template shares ONE token
  sink: { type: stdout, config: {} }
matrix:
  - { id: customers, source: { ref: ep, config: { path: /customers } } }
  - { id: orders,    source: { ref: ep, config: { path: /orders } } }
```

Provider `type:` values (catalog only): `static`, `oauth2` (client-credentials),
`oauth2_refresh` (with rotation), `token_endpoint`. A connector's `auth:` is
**either** an inline definition **or** a `{ ref }` — never both. See
`cli/examples/shared_auth_rest.yaml` for a full four-row example.

Shared providers are supported by the bearer/header-based connectors (rest,
graphql, xml, grpc, websocket, http sink, elasticsearch, snowflake-OAuth).

**Library use:** build one `faucet_auth` provider, wrap it in an `Arc`, and pass
it to each source/sink with `.with_auth_provider(provider.clone())`.

## Connector-specific inline auth

## Custom token endpoint

For non-standard token endpoints, `token_endpoint` lets you describe the request
and point at the access-token and expiry fields in the response. See
`faucet schema source rest` for the full field list.

Two knobs cover the less-standard flows:

- **`encoding: form`** sends the token request as
  `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (OAuth endpoints that expect a `resource=`
  param need this; the default is `json`).
- **`apply_as: { header, template }`** puts the fetched token in an arbitrary
  header instead of `Authorization: Bearer` — e.g. a session cookie. `template`
  is the header value with `{token}` substituted.

```yaml
auth:
  sap:                          # SAP B1: SessionId carried as a cookie
```

## Persisting a rotating refresh token

Some providers (Microsoft Graph, Rippling) **rotate the `refresh_token` on every
refresh** — the old one is invalidated. In-memory rotation works for a single
run, but the *next* scheduled run would present the now-stale seed and get a 401.
Set `persist.path` on an `oauth2_refresh` provider to durably store the rotated
token (a file-backed state store) so later runs pick up where the last one left
off:

```yaml
auth:
  graph:
    type: oauth2_refresh
    config:
      token_url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token"
      client_id: "${secret:graph_client_id}"
      client_secret: "${secret:graph_client_secret}"
      refresh_token: "${secret:graph_seed_refresh_token}"   # seed; used only until the first rotation
      persist:
        path: "./state/auth"      # rotated refresh_token survives across runs
```

## Custom token endpoint

For non-standard token endpoints, `token_endpoint` lets you describe the request
and point at the access-token and expiry fields in the response. See
`faucet schema source rest` for the full field list.

Two knobs cover the less-standard flows:

- **`encoding: form`** sends the token request as
  `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (OAuth endpoints that expect a `resource=`
  param need this; the default is `json`).
- **`apply_as: { header, template }`** puts the fetched token in an arbitrary
  header instead of `Authorization: Bearer` — e.g. a session cookie. `template`
  is the header value with `{token}` substituted.

```yaml
auth:
  sap:                          # SAP B1: SessionId carried as a cookie
    type: token_endpoint
    config:
      url: "https://host:50000/b1s/v1/Login"
      body: { CompanyDB: "${param.company_db}", UserName: "${param.user}", Password: "${secret:sap_pw}" }
      token_path: "$.SessionId"
      apply_as: { header: "Cookie", template: "B1SESSION={token}; CompanyDB=${param.company_db}" }
```

Some providers (Microsoft Graph, Rippling) **rotate the `refresh_token` on every
refresh** — the old one is invalidated. In-memory rotation works for a single
run, but the *next* scheduled run would present the now-stale seed and get a 401.
Set `persist.path` on an `oauth2_refresh` provider to durably store the rotated
token (a file-backed state store) so later runs pick up where the last one left
off:

```yaml

  graph:
    type: oauth2_refresh
    config:
      token_url: "https://login.microsoftonline.com/${param.tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token"
      client_id: "${secret:graph_client_id}"
      client_secret: "${secret:graph_client_secret}"
```
